subject.title: FRD: first-class multi-tenant RBAC (tenant claim on session/run/approval + tenant-scoped operator scopes + tenant-aware audit + fail-closed defaults)

question: Should OpenClaw make hostile same-gateway tenant isolation a first-class core security goal, or keep tenant isolation above the Gateway boundary?
rationale: The requested behavior changes OpenClaw's documented trust model and would add security-sensitive protocol, storage, approval, audit, and fail-closed config semantics that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Sponsor core threat-model design
options.body: Keep this issue open and have security/Gateway owners define the tenant boundary and decomposition before any implementation PR.

options.title: Reject core tenancy
options.body: Close the FRD after documenting that hostile tenant isolation remains a downstream platform boundary above OpenClaw Gateway.

options.title: Defer as future platform work
options.body: Leave the topic parked without implementation until there is maintainer capacity for a full security architecture pass.

recommendation.title: Sponsor core threat-model design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and have security/Gateway owners define the tenant boundary and decomposition before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: The security docs and trust-model history point to steipete as the strongest routing candidate for the boundary decision.
